key_insight: A physics-informed TabPFN can accurately predict frequency-dependent optical dielectric spectra of complex Mo-W-S-Se-Te TMD alloys from limited DFT data.
engineering_relevance: This enables rapid screening of compositionally tuned 2D optoelectronic materials without the cost of exhaustive first-principles calculations.
method: Generated 99 DFT alloy structures across binary to quinary Mo-W-S-Se-Te compositions.
Trained a tabular prior-fitted network on quaternary alloys using non-uniform, energy-focused physics-informed subsampling.
Predicted dielectric response and derived optical properties, then compared against Extra Trees and XGBoost baselines.
evidence_signal: Held-out quaternary alloys were reconstructed with R2 > 0.98 and MAE below 0.10 for all dielectric components, and quinary zero-shot predictions reached R2 > 0.97.
watch_item: The approach depends on carefully chosen energy subsampling and may be sensitive when extrapolating beyond the optically active region or outside the tested alloy space.
paper_title: Machine learning based prediction of optical properties in two-dimensional Mo-W-S-Se-Te transition-metal dichalcogenide alloys through physics-informed sampling
